1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.js  
   • This is the core implementation. It currently supports disabled, but does not accept a readOnly prop, nor does it apply a read-only CSS class, set aria-readonly, or suppress click/toggle behavior.  

2. packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.stories.js  
   • The Storybook file needs to expose the new readOnly prop in both the Default story (so users can copy/paste a read-only example) and the Playground story (so designers/developers can interactively toggle readOnly).  

3. packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle-test.js  
   • The unit tests must include RTL assertions for the readOnly variant: verifying that the read-only CSS class is applied, that aria-readonly is set on the switch, and that user clicks do not fire onClick or onToggle when readOnly is true.  

Together, these three files represent the minimal set that must be edited to implement, showcase, and validate the new read-only feature for the Toggle component.
1.bug_scenario:
The provided design screenshots show both the visual styling and structural spacing guidelines for a new “read-only” state of the Toggle component. 

• The first image (“Color and typography”) annotates the on/off text colors and icon colors for small and regular (big) toggles, including disabled and placeholder token references.  
• The second image (“Structure”) overlays exact pixel/rem spacing measurements for small and big toggles in their read-only state, indicating that the read-only variant should use the same dimensions and spacing as the enabled component but adopt the new styling and behavior.  

In short, the Toggle component needs a new readOnly prop that:  
1. Renders the component in a read-only style (per the color/typography tokens and spacing rules).  
2. Prevents value changes while still exposing the current state to screen readers.  
3. Integrates into the existing stories (default and playground) with controls.  
4. Is covered by RTL tests to assert the read-only class, absence of onToggle/onClick events, and proper ARIA attributes.
